mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for two months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in both the housing sector and consumer spending, which signals a broad-based economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or interaction term coefficient is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When manufacturing production falls below 95.0 (INDPRO < 95.0), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) above 1.0% signals robust economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 1.0% fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market contraction, which reduces consumer income and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining PAYEMS and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term coefficient is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.5%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
